blocks.p: A repeat asks the same questions again with the same settings and compares the letters with the first run. The published scores stay the first runs (the Vision tab's too); repeats are not ranked or summarised anywhere else.

The same 1,125 Logic and 2,163 Math questions in other forms, on the same load as a decision model's own run: options shuffled (two seeds), letters reversed (the first option becomes E), and in the “I don't know” run the words “I don't know” reworded. Each cell: the share of questions whose pick changes (compared by the option's content, not its letter) · the mean change of the probability given to the original pick, in percentage points. The reference is the standard run asked again unchanged on the same load (“Same again”, the noise floor; against the published run), or the published run where there is none; the reworded “I don't know” form is compared with the published “I don't know” run. Not part of any score.
